findings.message: The diff changes plugin code under plugins/specclaw (new hook, new bin, new lib, two new agents, edited templates and references) but bumps no version. None of the plugins/*/.claude-plugin/plugin.json, plugins/*/.codex-plugin/plugin.json or .claude-plugin/marketplace.json versions changed. Bump all of them to the same new version.
findings.scenario: A user on the previously released version updates the marketplace and sees no new version, so they never receive hooks/context-gate or the builder agents.

findings.message: last_context returns None when the transcript file does not exist, the same value it returns for 'no assistant call yet'. The hook then exits 0 in silence: no toast and no gate.jsonl line. If the transcript layout differs from the assumed `<session>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl`, the gate never fires and nothing says so. R2 still requires a gate error to be surfaced. Raise or log when a subagent's transcript is missing, and keep a silent pass only for a transcript that exists with no usage yet.
findings.scenario: An agent's transcript_path points at a layout where agent-<id>.jsonl is not found. The agent reaches 190k of its 200k cap and every call passes silently in warn and block mode. No log line or message shows the gate did not run.

findings.message: committing() splits the command on every `&`, so a stderr redirect such as `2>&1` or `>&2` leaves a fragment ('1', '2') that matches nothing in ALLOWED. A good-faith commit with a redirect is denied in block mode, so the agent cannot do the one thing the gate tells it to do. Strip fd redirects (`[0-9]*>&[0-9-]+`) before splitting, and add variant rows to the test: `git commit -m x 2>&1`, `git status 2>/dev/null`, `git log | head`.
findings.scenario: gate: block, agent at 95%, runs `git commit -m "wip" 2>&1`. The blanked command splits into ['git commit -m '' 2>', '1']. '1' fails ALLOWED, so the call is denied with exit 2 and the agent is locked out of committing.

findings.message: load() claims a bad budget value is a warning and the default stands. A blank `context:` under a role, or a non-scalar value, is parsed by _parse as `{}`. `{}` is not None, so `value.isdigit()` raises AttributeError. In the hook this fails open on every call. In `specclaw-budget roles --json` it is an uncaught traceback, since main() catches only ValueError and OSError. Treat a non-string value as a warning and keep the default.
findings.scenario:
config.yaml has `budget:
  roles:
    general:
      context:` (blank value). `specclaw-budget roles --json` dies with an AttributeError traceback instead of printing the four roles with a warning. The gate throws on every subagent call.

findings.message: estimate() skips any task without `Files:` before it looks at `Context:`. A task with a stated `Context: 90000` and no Files line is never flagged as over 60000.
findings.scenario: tasks.md has a task with `- Context: 90000` and no Files line. `estimate` prints nothing for it and exits 0 instead of 1.

findings.message: set_context writes to a fixed `config.yaml.tmp` name. Two concurrent sets (the dash and the CLI) collide on that file. A failed write leaves the tmp file behind. The new file also takes the default mode and not the original's. For `roles: {}` the rewrite drops the trailing comment, and the shipped template's `roles: {}  # ...` form is not in the set test, which uses a config without that line.
findings.scenario: `specclaw-budget set` on the shipped template turns `roles: {}  # set with ...` into `roles:` with the comment lost. A disk-full error leaves config.yaml.tmp beside config.yaml.
